description: PF3 on a re-entry: the third arm of the EVALUATE EIBAID at app/cbl/COUSR00C.cbl:122-137, reached at :125-127, and the only one of the twenty cases that drives it. The EVALUATE is ordered and the first match wins (gate G30): ENTER at :123, PF3 at :125, PF7 at :128, PF8 at :130 and WHEN OTHER at :132, so a case landing on the third arm is asserting that the two arms above it were tested and rejected. :126 moves 'COADM01C' into CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM and :127 performs RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN. RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN at :506-517 then runs in order: :508's test finds CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM already set, so :509's 'COSGN00C' default is NOT applied - which is the whole difference between this case and case01, where the same paragraph is entered with the field blank; :511 stamps CU00 into CDEMO-FROM-TRANID, :512 stamps COUSR00C into CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM, :513 moves ZEROS into CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT, and the XCTL at :514-517 transfers. The zeroed context is the load-bearing assertion here: it is the proof that the transfer really did reset the pseudo-conversation, so the next program starts in its own ENTER state at its own :115 rather than inheriting this one's re-entry. In the stateless projection the XCTL becomes the response's nextProgram and the client issues the follow-up call (gate G40, rule R6) - there is no server-side forward, no redirect chain and no session affinity - which is why termination is XCTL and not RETURN_TRANSID: control leaves at :517 and the EXEC CICS RETURN TRANSID('CU00') COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) at :141-144 is never reached on this path. WHAT THIS PATH DOES NOT DO, asserted positively rather than left unsaid. MAIN-PARA's prologue still runs first: :100-103 set ERR-FLG-OFF, USER-SEC-NOT-EOF, NEXT-PAGE-NO and SEND-ERASE-YES, :105-106 move SPACES to WS-MESSAGE and to ERRMSGO, and :108 moves -1 into USRIDINL - which is why cursorField is USRIDINL even though nothing is painted, the cursor request being made before the AID is ever examined. :121's RECEIVE does happen, because this is the re-entry branch, and then nothing on this path reads a single received field, so the case declares no mapFields: the operator's image is carried in the payload and discarded unread, and declaring values the run cannot consult would assert nothing while appearing to assert something. No map is sent. SEND-USRLST-SCREEN is reached from :119, :254, :276, :329, :377, :606, :613, :640, :647, :674 and :681 and none of those eleven sites is on this path, so 'sends' is empty rather than absent - the send count is behaviour, and zero is a value it takes. It follows that neither arm of :528-544 is exercised: :103 leaves WS-SEND-ERASE-FLG at its VALUE 'Y', but the SEND ... ERASE at :529-535 and the sibling at :537-543 whose ERASE operand is commented out at :541 are both unreached, so this case pins the ERASE choice by not reaching it at all. USRSEC is never opened: no STARTBR (:586), no READNEXT (:619), no READPREV (:653) and no ENDBR (:687), which makes this a meaningful negative entry in the access-path matrix (gate G47) rather than a case that merely happens not to browse. No page arithmetic fires either - not :304, not :309-310, not :320-321, not :358, not :367 and not :369 - so CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM leaves exactly as it arrived (gate G28), and neither INITIALIZE-USER-DATA (:446-501) nor POPULATE-USER-DATA (:384-441) is performed. The dead WS-USER-DATA array at :56-64, an OCCURS 10 table the program declares and never once references, stays unmodelled (practice B5). THE RESPONSE. All twenty-two communication-area fields are pinned: the sixteen of app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy:19-44, whose spans sum to 160, plus all six of the 34-byte CDEMO-CU00-INFO extension declared at :67-75 as 8+8+8+1+1+8. The two together are the 194 bytes EIBCALEN reports, and the extension is 34 and not 58 - COTRN00C's equivalent is 58 and is not copied here. Every field the request did not declare is pinned at WORKING-STORAGE's initial state, spaces for an alphanumeric item and zeros for a PIC 9 one, because :114's MOVE DFHCOMMAREA(1:EIBCALEN) copies in only what the client sent; CDEMO-CU00-NEXT-PAGE-FLG is accordingly the VALUE 'N' it is declared with at :71 and not a value this path computed. expectedMessages is empty: no DISPLAY is reached, the three DISPLAY sites at :608, :642 and :676 all being WHEN OTHER arms of a browse this case never starts, and no screen is painted, so there is no ERRMSGO image either. Screen text belongs in a send's fields under this contract and this list carries only lines a program emits, so an empty list here is the accurate statement rather than an omission. expectedReturnCode is 0, and holds for all twenty cases: the program contains no MOVE ... TO RETURN-CODE and no CALL 'CEE3ABD'. THE FILE. USRSEC is untouched, and saying so precisely is most of this case's value. Each of the ten rows is pinned BOTH field by field, in app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy:17-23 declaration order with SEC-USR-FILLER NAMED because the copybook names it at :23 rather than leaving it anonymous, AND as the whole 80-byte image - so the values, the total width, and the filler having been emitted as spaces rather than as zeros or not at all are three separate assertions (gates G19, G21). A record missing its filler is short by exactly that span, which is why the image is pinned alongside the fields and not instead of them. The offsets are summed mechanically rather than asserted in prose (practice B11): 8+20+20+8+1 = 57, plus the NAMED SEC-USR-FILLER X(23) makes 80, and app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl fixes that 80 twice independently - at :48 with DCB=(LRECL=80,RECFM=FB) and again in its IDCAMS DEFINE CLUSTER with RECORDSIZE(80,80) KEYS(8,0). expectedDatasets then adds the one statement no row expectation can make: on the FINAL_STATE channel USRSEC still holds exactly ten rows at that 80-byte width. Ten pinned rows cannot say that an eleventh was not added, and 'the transfer touched nothing' is precisely a claim about the count as well as the contents. SEED. USRSEC has no ASCII fixture - app/data/ASCII holds nine files and none of them is a security-user file - so its rows are always inline, and no tenth fixture is requested. All ten here are VERBATIM in-stream records of app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44 at their in-stream width of exactly 57 characters, and none is synthesized; the synthesized extensions that exist to carry the ten-row page boundary belong to the paging cases, and this path reads no record at all. No row is pre-padded: the 23-byte shortfall is the absent SEC-USR-FILLER, and it is carried to 80 once, at seed time, by the single USRSEC_FILLER_PAD_57_TO_80 normalisation declared below, which the harness and FieldDiffer own between them. SEC-USR-PWD stays the plaintext eight-character literal the legacy design stores and compares (practice B6) - hashing, masking or omitting it would change what this contract asserts - and it never reaches a screen on any path, least of all this one, which paints nothing. CONVENTIONS. jobParameters is OMITTED rather than declared empty: COUSR00C is not a batch job and takes no JCL PARM, and ParityCase refuses a job parameter for any unitKind but BATCH_JOB, so the three conversation scalars travel as screenRequest.eibcalen, screenRequest.aid and screenRequest.commarea['CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT'] instead - which is also how gate G37 and rule R6 are met, since no server-side session state exists anywhere in the path for the conversation to have been remembered in. The code page is named US-ASCII explicitly and never defaulted (practice B8), and spaces are written as spaces and kept distinct from the LOW-VALUES that :117 moves into COUSR0AO on the first-entry branch this case does not take. The clock is pinned to 2022-07-19T23:12:34, the source's own version stamp rather than an invented instant, because POPULATE-HEADER-INFO calls FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE at :564 on every send and an unpinned header would make a case irreproducible; this path sends nothing, so the value is carried for uniformity rather than asserted (practice B7). USRSEC is addressed by its binding key throughout and never by a dataset name (gate G46); app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:88-99 defines FILE(USRSEC) with ADD, BROWSE, DELETE, READ and UPDATE, and this program uses browse alone. Page size ten is BEHAVIOUR and not configuration (gate G39): it is hard-coded at :293, :300, :347 and :352 and by 02 USER-REC OCCURS 10 TIMES at :57, it is not consulted on this path, and no page-size value appears anywhere in this file. No attribute or colour item is declared, because the program moves none: COUSR00C copies COCOM01Y, COUSR00, COTTL01Y, CSDAT01Y, CSMSG01Y, CSUSR01Y, DFHAID and DFHBMSCA at :66-84 and copies neither DFHATTR nor CSSETATY, so there is no runtime DFHRED and no '*' overwrite to assert; ERRMSG is statically COLOR=RED, ATTRB=(ASKIP,BRT,FSET) in app/bms/COUSR00.bms, and inventing a highlight here would have been a new behaviour (gate G38, which this case meets on its REENTER side). Not applicable and deliberately not fabricated: gate G32, since this program contains no GO TO; gate G35, since it contains no CALL 'CEE3ABD'; and gate G43, since it has no 9300-CHECK-CHANGE-IN-REC. RULE R1. The plan mandates the class name UserMenuController, but the Function header at app/cbl/COUSR00C.cbl:5 reads 'List all users from USRSEC file', app/bms/COUSR00.bms paints 'List Users', and README.md records CU00 the same way. The name comes from the plan and the behaviour from the source: this is a paginated list screen, and nothing here expects menu-shaped behaviour. SCENARIO DIVERGENCE, recorded rather than silently resolved (practice B4, and the same protocol the plan applies to its own conflicts). The file-level brief for case11 described a different scenario: PF8 pressed with CDEMO-CU00-NEXT-PAGE-FLG at 'N', taking the else limb of :270 and painting the 44-character 'You are already at the bottom of the page...' of :273-274 through the ERASE-suppressed send of :537-543. That arm is real and it is already pinned - by case09, which declares DFHPF8 with the flag arriving 'N' and whose message literal this suite asserts verbatim - whereas case11 is the ONLY one of the twenty cases that declares DFHPF3. Re-pointing it would therefore have deleted the sole parity coverage of the WHEN DFHPF3 arm at :125-127 and of RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN entered with CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM already set, and it would have left the suite's AID-matrix assertion - that ENTER, PF3, PF7 and PF8 are each driven, gates G30 and G38 - unable to hold. Behaviour is taken from the source and the case keeps its DFHPF3 identity, exactly as rule R1 directs for the sixteen class names whose labels diverge from what their sources do. What the brief additionally required of a case file is delivered here in full: the ordered eighty-byte field maps with the named filler, the dataset-level row count that makes 'unmutated' an assertion, and this provenance paragraph. PROVENANCE (practice B12, risk R-A): every expected value here was DERIVED BY STRUCTURED READING of the COBOL and its copybooks and was NOT captured from, recorded against or replayed from any execution of the legacy program - executing it is impossible in this environment, which has no z/OS or CICS runtime, whose COBOL compiler reports its indexed file handler disabled, which provides no Language Environment CEE* services, and which is missing the IBM-supplied DFHAID and DFHBMSCA the program copies at :83-84. Only the provenance of the expected values is substituted; the twenty cases per program, the field-for-field diffing and the diff-count-of-zero gate per module are all preserved unchanged, and because a statically derived expectation can encode a misreading where a captured one could not, every width and offset above is taken mechanically from a copybook rather than from prose. The derivation rests on app/cbl/COUSR00C.cbl:56-84, :98-144, :149-232, :237-277, :282-331, :336-379, :384-441, :446-501, :506-517, :522-544, :549-557, :562-581 and :586-695; app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy:19-44, whose spans sum to 160; app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy:17-23, whose 8+20+20+8+1 = 57 plus the NAMED SEC-USR-FILLER X(23) make 80; app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy, whose two forty-character titles this path never paints; app/cpy-bms/COUSR00.CPY, whose 59 xxxI items fix every screen field name and width and whose 01 COUSR0AO REDEFINES COUSR0AI at :373 is why the program populates input items and sends from the output view; and app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44 and :48.
